title: Postmortem-to-QBR Translation and Customer Readout Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a repeatable process for turning internal incident postmortem findings into a concise, customer-facing QBR (Quarterly Business Review) narrative and readout. The goal is to:
- Surface root causes and mitigations in a way that maps to customer SLAs/SLOs and business impact.
- Provide a clear, action-oriented plan customers can review and sign off on.
- Standardize the rhythm and artifacts for CS-led incident readouts so engineering, SRE, and account teams stay aligned.

When to use this playbook:
1) Any incident that triggered a postmortem with customer-visible impact (latency SLO breach, model-quality regression, outage affecting >1% of tenant traffic, billing anomalies tied to runaway token usage).
2) Major configuration or migration failures that change expected behaviour for a customer.
3) Recurring or high-severity issues flagged by the Customer Success or Enterprise Support teams.

Scope and audience:
- Primary audience: Customer Success Manager (CSM), Account Executive (AE), Engineering Lead on the incident, and the affected customer’s technical stakeholders.
- Secondary audience: SRE, Product PM, and Support.

High-level process overview:
1) Postmortem author finalizes root-cause analysis and mitigation items.
2) CS partner maps technical findings to customer-facing metrics and prepares readout slide deck.
3) Joint internal rehearsal with engineering and CS to agree on messaging and acceptance criteria.
4) Customer readout meeting and follow-up commit list.
5) Tracking through to closure; reflect changes in the next QBR.

Roles and responsibilities (quick reference):
- Postmortem Author (Engineering): Produce final postmortem doc, timeline of events, RCA, impact window, and proposed technical mitigations.
- SRE/Oncall Lead: Confirm artifact accuracy (metrics, graphs, SLO timelines) and sign off on planned mitigations and rollbacks.
- CSM (Owner of Readout): Draft customer narrative, schedule readout, lead the meeting, and maintain follow-up tracker.
- AE: Coordinate customer commercial expectations and any contractual communications.
- Product PM: Provide roadmap context for long-term fixes and prioritization.

Minimum artifact checklist (required before scheduling a customer readout):
- Final internal postmortem (link) with clear RCA and timeline.
- Impact table (customers, tenant IDs, affected routes/endpoints, time windows).
- SLO/SLA graph(s) showing deviation and recovery (PNG/SVG).
- Action items table with owners, due dates, and verification steps.
- Customer-facing 6-slide deck (template below).

6-slide customer readout deck template (concise):
1) Title slide: incident name, customer, date, presenters.
2) Executive summary: one-sentence outcome, one-sentence customer impact, and current status.
3) What happened: brief timeline and root cause (non-technical summary first, technical appendix as follow-up).
4) Impact on your service: mapped to the customer’s SLOs/usage and any financial impact or credits.
5) Actions we took and next steps: short-term mitigations and planned long-term fixes with target dates.
6) Ask of the customer and close: verification plan, acceptance criteria, and scheduled follow-up checkpoint.

Translating technical findings into QBR metrics (mapping guide):
- Latency spike -> translate to: percentage of requests > 2x SLO, P95 and P99 delta vs baseline, affected endpoints, and customer business flows impacted (e.g., search, generation).
- Model-quality regression -> translate to: evaluation testset delta (accuracy/score), customer-facing examples (before/after), percentage of calls classified as ‘regression’ by monitoring rules, and remediation confidence level.
- Partial availability / degraded throughput -> translate to: minutes of reduced capacity, number of failed/queued requests, and effective availability percentage for the customer during the window.
- Cost anomaly -> translate to: additional token spend, specific prompt patterns, tenant configuration that caused increase, and recommended guardrails.

Customer readout runbook (step-by-step):
1) Internal sign-off (T-72h): postmortem author and SRE sign the artifacts. CSM schedules the readout with customer and internal stakeholders.
2) Draft deck (T-48h): CSM drafts slides using the 6-slide template; include appendices with graphs and raw query samples.
3) Rehearsal (T-24h): 30–45 minute dry run with engineering and AE to align on answers to likely questions (root cause, regression probability, rollback options, ETA for fix).
4) Readout meeting: 30–45 minutes max. Suggested agenda: 5m exec summary, 10m technical but non-dense timeline, 10m actions and verification plan, 10m Q&A + next steps. Keep the readout focused on outcomes and customer verification.
5) Post-readout (within 48h): CSM publishes the slide deck and the public-friendly incident summary to the customer. Create/update a follow-up tracker in the customer’s onboarding board.
6) Checkpoint (T+14 days): Verify short-term mitigations; engineering provides status update and evidence (metrics, synthetic runs).
7) QBR inclusion (next scheduled QBR): One slide summarizing the incident, impact, mitigations completed, and remaining open items with owners.

Acceptance criteria for customer sign-off (examples):
- Short-term mitigation validated by both engineering (SRE) and customer via agreed synthetic test (pass criteria: <X% error over 24h; configurable per customer).
- Long-term fix scheduled into product/infra backlog with a committed target quarter and owner assigned.
- Any commercial remediation (credits, SLA adjustments) agreed and captured in the renewal/billing system.

Templates and language guidance (do/don’t):
- Do: Use plain language first, then technical appendix. Lead with the impact to the customer and what we have done about it.
- Do: Provide concrete verification (metrics, test names, runbook checks).
- Don’t: Overuse internal jargon in the customer-facing slides. Avoid speculative language (e.g., 'probably', 'might').
- Don’t: Dump raw logs into the readout — include curated examples in the appendix instead.

Example translation (short):
Internal postmortem finding: "KV cache eviction race under heavy prefix fanout caused N+1 model loads between 11:12–11:41 UTC, increasing P99 latency from 420ms to 1.8s for /v1/stream."
Customer QBR translation: "Between 11:12–11:41 UTC we observed a cache coordination issue that temporarily increased tail latency for streaming responses used by your search feature. Approximately 3.2% of requests served hit the degraded window, resulting in elevated P99 (1.8s vs normal 0.42s). We deployed config changes (KV cache backoff and faster rehydration) and are monitoring; a long-term fix (improved cache coordination and bakeoff) is scheduled for the next release. A synthetic test is in place and will be shared for customer verification."

Communication templates (short):
- Readout invite subject: "Readout: [Incident name] — impact summary and next steps"
- Readout invite body: "Hi <Customer>, we’d like to schedule a 30-minute readout to review the incident on <date>. We will cover impact, immediate mitigations, and proposed next steps. Please invite any technical stakeholders who should sign off on the verification plan."
- Post-readout email subject: "Follow-up: [Incident name] — artifacts and verification plan"

Tracking and verification fields (example table - store in customer board):
- item_id | short_description | owner | due_date | verification_method | status
- PM-101 | KV cache fix scheduled | Eng-Cache | 2026-12-15 | E2E synthetic v2 pass | open
- CS-202 | Customer synthetic verification | CSM-Jane | 2026-11-30 | Shared test run and screenshot | in_progress

Escalation and sensitivity notes:
- If the incident has regulatory or data-exposure implications, escalate to Security and Legal immediately and adjust customer messaging to ‘restricted’ confidentiality.
- For incidents with contractual SLA impacts, involve Finance and Sales leaders before the readout to pre-clear commercial remediation options.

Metrics and artifacts to attach to the readout (required):
- Tenant-level availability and latency time series (P50/P95/P99).
- Synthetic test results before/after mitigation.
- Short curated log snippets and query samples (appendix).
- Postmortem link and the public-friendly incident summary.

Follow-up governance and closure criteria:
- All action items must have owners and dates and be tracked in the customer’s board.
- CSM verifies short-term mitigations within 14 days and marks the checklist items green when verified.
- Long-term fixes are tracked quarterly; any slip requires notification in the next scheduled QBR.

Related playbooks and templates:
- QBR slide templates (internal asset link)
- Incident postmortem template (eng-sre)
- Customer synthetic validation guide (integration-guides)

Appendix: Example Q&A prep (anticipated questions and suggested answers):
Q: "How likely is recurrence?"
A: "We have applied a short-term mitigation that reduces the known attack surface and put a synthetic monitor in place. Probability is low in the short term; the long-term fix will remove the root cause and is scheduled for Q1. We will provide a confidence update after the T+14 validation."

Q: "Will my usage bill be affected?"
A: "We have evaluated the token spend impact for the incident window and will surface any credit recommendation if the customer experienced material additional cost. Commercial remediation requires AE and Finance approval and will be captured in the follow-up tracker."

Document ownership and updates:
Owner: Customer Success (CSM guild).
Update cadence: Review after every readout that includes technical incidents; refresh template quarterly or when guidance changes.

End of playbook.
